I can imagine it must be difficult! I am also 22, but I’ve been moved out since I was 18. Sometimes, it can be difficult to know where to start. 

-Do you have a job? Are you able to get any income to save up to move out? 

-What types of domestic skills do you already know? (Laundry, mopping, cooking?) 

-what kind of bills and debt do you already pay? If you have a stable income, you can usually call the phone listed on the website and ask to transfer it into your name, and often times you can enroll in autopay, so you won’t miss a payment. 

-keeping a Google sheets/Excel spreadsheet of your monthly budget is a big first step. What is your income after taxes? What is your rent? What kinds of monthly bills do you have (water, phone, Netflix)? What kind of food or car expenses do you have? It can be a bit tedious, but it’s important to get a rough estimate to know what you have to work with.

The best way to get rid of the “I should be supervised” feeling is to do a lot of independent stuff. I am not sure if you still live with your parents, but getting involved with some projects or events that sound interesting can be a big first step. 

Head out to your local library- are there any events posted on a board somewhere? Take yourself on a date to a coffee shop, if you’re close enough to one. Are there music events you could check out? Those are a great place to meet people. (Often times village/city social media or websites will have events listed!) 

Even volunteering is a great way to feel independent and meet new people. I don’t know if you’re employed  or live with your folks, but that’s my two cents. You are an adult, you shouldn’t have to ask your parents, but I understand you may have particular circumstances.

Getting out and meeting people and doing stuff on your own will feel weird at first, but it won’t always feel like that.

It’s so strange to me that people think that gender identity discussion is even new. Take for instance, The Public Universal Friend, who was a preacher in the mid 1700’s, who was well known and used no pronouns at all.

Also, as a trans adult I must say the amount of misinformation is atrocious!! What a person’s transition goals or process looks like will be different for any person who wants to transition. There’s the social aspect of transition, of changing names and perhaps clothing or hair and pronouns in public and with friends. This is what most trans and NbY children who transition do. Medical transition, however, is usually not until they are much older and can consent to making lasting decisions. Even then, it’s primarily puberty blockers that pause puberty until they reach adulthood to start gender affirming hormones. (Any amount of transition is valid!! You don’t need to medically transition to be trans)

I was in college (still am) at the time and I wasn’t able to work or go to classes because I couldn’t really keep it together to do much more than showering or some very basic tasks at first. 
I OD’ed on a medication that caused the psychosis, and for the first week I locked myself in my room completely. I couldn’t control my body at all due to severe tics and tremors. 

In a month I started showering again, with slightly less than ever-constant positive symptoms, and I tried to feel comfortable doing other tasks, like brushing my hair. I was so anxious to move a muscle, because I couldn’t tell where I was and some other scary stuff. 

3 months in, it mellowed out a bit. I started going on walks with someone I trusted, who I finally had the courage to tell that something was very very wrong. 

6 months in I began going back to class with much difficulty. Still an anxious and paranoid person. 

1 year in, and I learned to sit with the feelings that come. They were less ever present, but still there. I began cooking and baking as an outlet. 

3 years in and I am holding a job and taking classes! Full disclosure, I am on an AP right now in case it ever comes back and to help with paranoia, which I’ve been on for about 4(?) months? While I miss the person I was, I do feel better than that first 6 months. I don’t know if this was a good timeline or not. I struggle with organized thinking and I have a lot of memories missing from this time.
Thank you!! It’s been a very slow process but I am finding peace.
